::: {.lead}
My work spans infinite-distance limits, emergent strings, quantum corrections,
asymptotic Hodge theory, flux vacua, and mathematical structures in integrable models.
My name is shown in **bold** below.
:::

### Quantum obstructions for $\mathcal{N}=1$ infinite-distance limits — Part II: Kähler obstructions

L. Kaufmann, **J. Monnee**, T. Weigand, and M. Wiesner

*Physical Review D* **113**, 126028 (2026)

::: {.pub-summary}
Complex-structure limits generically backreact on the Kähler sector. Worldsheet and
instanton arguments show that correlated scaling is required to retain perturbative control.
:::

### Quantum obstructions for $\mathcal{N}=1$ infinite-distance limits — Part I: $g_s$ obstructions

L. Kaufmann, **J. Monnee**, T. Weigand, and M. Wiesner

*Physical Review D* **113**, 126027 (2026)

::: {.pub-summary}
Non-perturbative string-coupling effects can become unsuppressed and can substantially
modify, or in extreme cases remove, classical infinite-distance degenerations.

**J. Monnee**, T. Weigand, and M. Wiesner

**J. Monnee**, T. Weigand, and M. Wiesner

*Journal of High Energy Physics* **03**, 063 (2026)

B. Hassfeld, **J. Monnee**, T. Weigand, and M. Wiesner

*Journal of High Energy Physics* **01**, 140 (2026)

### Deformed WZW models and Hodge theory — Part I

T. W. Grimm and **J. Monnee**

*Journal of High Energy Physics* **05**, 103 (2022)

::: {.pub-summary}
A class of solutions in deformed WZW models is shown to describe variations of
Hodge structure, connecting integrable models to period mappings.

### Bulk reconstruction in moduli-space holography

T. W. Grimm, **J. Monnee**, and D. van de Heisteeg

*Journal of High Energy Physics* **05**, 010 (2022)

::: {.pub-summary}
Near-boundary solutions are reconstructed from $SL(2)$ boundary data using recursion
relations originating in the proof of the $SL(2)$-orbit theorem.
:::
